data.name: Saudi Arabia
data.summary: No individual income tax scheme: a private investor's portfolio gains, dividends and interest are not taxed, and there is no inheritance, gift or wealth tax. Saudi and GCC nationals pay Zakat (2.5% of the Zakat base) on business holdings; foreign-owned business profits pay 20% income tax. Real Estate Transaction Tax 5% on property disposals; VAT 15%; 2.5% annual white land tax on qualifying vacant urban land. Residency for wealthy foreigners via Premium Residency. About 58 treaties, none with the US.

regimes.name: Saudi Arabia tax residence
regimes.description: No personal income tax; Zakat applies to Saudi/GCC nationals' business holdings only.
regimes.eligibility: Any legal resident (Premium Residency or employment).

capital_gains.summary: No tax on capital gains for a private individual investor. Business income (including gains) is taxed at entity/PE level: 20% income tax for the non-Saudi share, Zakat for the Saudi/GCC share.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Disposal of Saudi real estate bears 5% Real Estate Transaction Tax on the full disposal value (also on transfers of real-estate-rich entities); this is a transaction tax, not a gains tax. A non-Saudi individual selling shares in an unlisted Saudi company may be taxed at 20% on the gain under the Income Tax Law; not verified, and not relevant for a foreign private business.

capital_gains.rate_basis: No individual income tax scheme (PwC). Gains realised in a business are subject to income tax or Zakat at the normal rates (PwC corporate); disposals of shares listed on the Saudi Exchange are exempt subject to conditions.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Activity amounting to a business carried on in Saudi Arabia is taxed at the business level (20% income tax for non-Saudis).

dividends.summary: No tax on dividends received by individuals.

dividends.treaty_network: About 58 treaty partners listed by PwC; no treaty with the United States, so US dividends held directly bear 30% US WHT.

wealth_tax.summary: No net wealth tax. Zakat on Saudi/GCC nationals is assessed on business/company Zakat bases, not on a foreign family's personal portfolio.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: No general property tax. White land tax: 2.5% a year of market value on qualifying vacant urban land zoned residential or commercial.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance, estate or gift tax.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Succession, not tax, is the issue: personal status (family) law based on Sharia governs inheritance of Muslims, with fixed shares (a son typically takes twice a daughter's share) and at most one third freely disposable by will to non-heirs. How estates of non-Muslim foreigners are handled (home-country law, own religious rules, or Sharia by default) was not verified for this country; non-Muslim families should take local legal advice and hold portfolio assets outside the country or through a structure with a clear governing law. Saudi courts apply Sharia; the 2022 Personal Status Law codified it (not opened).

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident if the individual has a permanent home in Saudi Arabia and is present at least 30 days in the year, or is present at least 183 days in the year; part days count as full days (PwC). Relevant only for business income, since there is no personal income tax.

income.name: Saudi Arabia

income_tax.summary: There is no individual income tax scheme in Saudi Arabia; employment income is untaxed (PwC, reviewed 29 Jul 2026). Non-employment income is taxed under entity/permanent-establishment rules. Non-Saudi employees pay no GOSI contribution (the 2% occupational-hazard charge is borne by the employer); Saudi employees pay 9.75% (9% plus 0.75% SANED).
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Self-employed contributions not covered by PwC. A freelancer's non-employment income can fall under the entity (corporate) rules rather than personal tax; the 20% foreign-owned profit tax is noted in the existing jurisdiction file.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local income-based taxes. Saudi employees' GOSI base is basic salary plus housing, capped at SAR 45,000 a month.

succession.name: Saudi Arabia
succession.summary: Sharia fixed shares apply, with a bequest of up to one third and none to an existing heir without the others' consent (Personal Status Law, Royal Decree M/73). Non-Muslim foreigners' treatment is unsettled in the sources. Courts do not recognise trusts; family waqf is the onshore alternative.
succession.reserved_share: Fixed Sharia shares after debts and funeral costs; a bequest limited to one third and not to an existing heir unless the other heirs consent; heirs must share the deceased's religion (Personal Status Law 2022, as described by a practitioner guide).
succession.foreign_law_note: Sources conflict: one says non-Muslims' estates may follow home-country law by agreement of heirs, with disputes decided by Saudi courts applying Sharia; another says Sharia applies unless offshore structures are used.
succession.trust_note: Saudi courts reportedly do not recognise foreign trusts and give effect to the registered legal owner. Waqf (Islamic endowment) is the onshore vehicle, with offshore foundations suggested by advisers (commercial advice, not law). No private-foundation statute was found.
open_questions: Saudi conflict-of-laws rule for foreigners' estates not confirmed from legislation.
Waqf rules and whether a family waqf can benefit chosen heirs not researched.
All sources are practitioner guides, not the Royal Decree text.

Hague Trusts Convention: The HCCH status table (checked 2026-10-16) lists 14 Contracting Parties; this country is not one of them and no UK, Dutch or Chinese extension covers it, so the 1985 Convention is not in force here.

immigration.name: Saudi Arabia
immigration.summary: No free movement for anyone; EU, US and other passports use the same Premium Residency products run by the Premium Residency Center. The cheapest is the Real Estate Owner residency (property of SAR 4,000,000), then the annual Limited Duration product (SAR 100,000 a year); permanent status costs SAR 800,000 once or SAR 7,000,000 invested with 10 jobs. No remote-work visa exists. Citizenship is by decree only.
immigration.naturalisation: Not researched from the Saudi Citizenship System in this pass. Premium Residency does not lead to citizenship automatically.
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: General rule, not verified in this pass: dual nationality needs government permission.

routes.name: Premium Residency - Unlimited Duration
routes.summary: A one-off payment of SAR 800,000 buys permanent residence without a sponsor.
routes.requirements: Premium Residency Center product: one-time fee SAR 800,000, permanent; age 21+, proof of financial capability, passport valid 6 months. The fee is paid, not invested. Terms are taken from consultancy guides because pr.gov.sa could not be read.
routes.fees_note: Product fee. A separate application processing fee of about USD 170 is reported (KSA Expats).
routes.tax_note: Saudi has no personal income tax on individuals' earned or investment income; see jurisdiction file.

routes.name: Premium Residency - Real Estate Owner
routes.summary: Owning residential property worth at least SAR 4,000,000 gives residency for as long as you hold it.
routes.requirements: Property worth at least SAR 4,000,000, completed, residential, unmortgaged, valued by a Taqeem-accredited valuer (off-plan from a RERA-approved developer allowed with a down payment of the higher of SAR 1,000,000 or 10%, no financing). Residency lasts while the property or usufruct is held; does not convert to permanent. A law letting foreigners buy in approved projects took effect 28 January 2026 (press report); approved areas and details were still pending.
routes.fees_note: Product fee SAR 4,000; processing fee about USD 170 reported separately.
routes.physical_presence: Not required to live in the property (press).

routes.name: Premium Residency - Investor
routes.summary: Invest SAR 7,000,000 in a Saudi business and create 10 jobs in two years for permanent residence.
routes.requirements: Product requirements: at least SAR 7,000,000 invested capital (owner share), 10 jobs within the first two years, Ministry of Investment licence and commercial registration. Direct permanent residence conditional on meeting the targets during the first two years.

routes.name: Premium Residency - Entrepreneur (two categories)
routes.summary: Start-up founders backed by an approved investor get 5 years, or permanent residence for a SAR 15,000,000 venture with 20 jobs.
routes.requirements: Category 1: entrepreneur licence from the Ministry of Investment, funding round of at least SAR 400,000 from an approved investor, at least 20% ownership, 5 years renewable (renewal needs 30 months of residence). Category 2: at least SAR 15,000,000 funding, at least 10% ownership, 10 jobs in year 1 and 10 more in year 2, permanent conditional.
routes.investment_options: Category 2: SAR 15,000,000 and 20 jobs for permanent residence.
routes.physical_presence: 30 months in the 5 years for renewal of Category 1.

routes.name: Premium Residency - Special Talent and Gifted
routes.summary: Residence for employed specialists (researchers, doctors, executives) and for people with exceptional artistic or sporting achievements.
routes.requirements: Special Talent: employment with a listed entity, bachelor's degree, 3+ years of experience, monthly pay of at least SAR 14,000 (researchers), SAR 35,000 (health and science), SAR 80,000 (executives). Gifted: nomination or award and a recommendation from the Ministry of Culture or Sports. 5 years, renewable once; permanent after 30 months of residence within 5 years.
routes.physical_presence: 30 months of residence within the 5 years for permanent status.

routes.requirements: Employer sponsorship through the Ministry of Human Resources and Absher/Muqeem; Saudisation quotas apply. Not researched in detail.
routes.physical_presence: Residence lapses after prolonged absence outside the Kingdom (not verified).
